learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the economy of the universe! Learn how forces do work, how energy is transferred and conserved, and how power measures the speed of work.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: In physics, work is only done when a force causes displacement. It is the dot product of Force and Displacement vectors: $W = \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{d} = Fd\cos\theta$. If you push a wall and it doesn't move, your physics work is zero!
Kinetic Energy ($K = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$) is the energy of motion. Potential Energy ($U = mgh$) is stored energy due to position or configuration (like a stretched spring: $U = \frac{1}{2}kx^2$).
A beautiful link: The net work done by ALL forces acting on a body is exactly equal to the change in its kinetic energy. ($W_{net} = K_f - K_i$).
If only conservative forces (like gravity or spring force) are doing work, the total mechanical energy (Kinetic + Potential) of the system remains perfectly constant at every point in the motion.

When objects crash! In an 'Elastic Collision', both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved (like billiard balls). In an 'Inelastic Collision', momentum is conserved but some kinetic energy is lost as heat or sound (like car crashes).

fun_activity.title: pendulum The Bowling Ball Pendulum
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine a heavy pendulum pulled back to your nose and released. If you don't lean forward, it will swing out and come back to stop exactly at your nose, never hitting you. Why? Conservation of Mechanical Energy! It cannot gain more height/energy than it started with.

exam_tips: 📌 Work is zero if the force is exactly perpendicular ($90^\circ$) to the displacement (e.g., a porter carrying a load on his head walking horizontally).
📌 The area under a Force-Position ($F-x$) graph directly gives the total Work Done.
📌 Memorize the formulas for final velocities in a 1D elastic collision. They are frequently used in complex 5-mark numericals.
quick_recap: ⭐ The dot product of two vectors yields a scalar. Therefore, Work is a scalar quantity even though Force and Displacement are vectors.
⭐ Power is the rate of doing work: $P = W/t$. 1 Horsepower (HP) = 746 Watts.
⭐ Friction is a non-conservative force; the work done by friction depends entirely on the path taken.
